routes.description: Show that belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God is not proportioned to the available reason and evidence, notwithstanding possible defenses or generic creator arguments.
routes.successCriteria: Establish that apparently gratuitous evil or salvation confusion materially defeats rational classical theism, or that the con case fails to supply evidence strong enough to overcome those defeaters.

bridges.description: The full evidential balance makes classical theistic belief irrational.
Apparently gratuitous suffering conflicts with unlimited power and love.
High-stakes but culturally confused salvation requirements conflict with divine love.
Naturalistic cognition is not shown to be globally self-defeating.
Natural explanations weaken an inference from apparent design to God.
Evolutionary genealogy and the Euthyphro dilemma challenge divine moral grounding.

routes.description: Show cumulatively that rational cognition, cosmic fine-tuning, and objective morality favor God, while suffering remains serious counterevidence rather than a decisive defeater.
routes.successCriteria: Supply a coherent evidential route making God more probable than nonexistence and show that the evil objection does not eliminate rational theistic belief.

bridges.description: The cumulative evidential case makes belief in God rational overall.
A rational creator better explains generally truth-directed human cognition.
Life-permitting fine-tuning is substantially more probable given intelligent design.
Objective moral obligations are best grounded in the nature of God.
Afterlife, theodicy, and divine participation prevent evil from defeating theism.
Guided evolution preserves intention and human purpose without rejecting natural selection.

sections.title: Gratuitous evil and theodicy
sections.rationale: This is the pro side's principal case and the strongest counterevidence expressly conceded by the con side.

sections.title: Salvation confusion and hiddenness
sections.rationale: This is a distinct pro argument connecting divine love to disputed, culturally variable, high-stakes belief conditions.

sections.title: Rational cognition and naturalism
sections.rationale: The con side makes cognitive reliability a central positive argument, followed by sustained direct exchange over evolution and epistemic parity.

sections.title: Fine-tuning and design
sections.rationale: Fine-tuning is one of the con side's three cumulative constructives, although it receives little direct engagement during the moderated exchange.

sections.title: Moral facts, genealogy, and grounding
sections.rationale: Both sides devote substantial argument and reply time to moral intuition, evolutionary genealogy, normativity, and the Euthyphro dilemma.
